analysis.explanation: For folder opening (10k files), the primary lag is located in MAIN_PROCESS_FS (51.4ms), caused by sequential asynchronous directory walks and filesystem stats across deep folder trees. This is immediately followed by IPC_PAYLOAD (70.4ms) due to the monolithic 2.19MB nested JSON tree shape. Conversely, for large file opening (1MB), the primary lag shifts to RENDERER_PAINT (1.2ms), driven by Monaco text model creation, line offset indexing, and bracket token parsing on the UI thread. Additionally, 26 synchronous filesystem calls were flagged in main handlers, including synchronous disk writes in recent-workspaces.ts.

findingsBySubsystem.mainProcessFs: S2 Directory walk takes 51.4ms for 10k files. Synchronous fs.writeFileSync in recent-workspaces.ts:75 blocks the main process event loop.
findingsBySubsystem.ipcPayload: 10k folder tree produces 2.19MB JSON payload in fs:get-tree, exceeding the 2MB threshold. S3+S4 serialization and IPC transfer total 70.4ms.
findingsBySubsystem.rendererPaint: VirtualFileTree flattening takes 0.8ms on the UI thread. Opening a 1MB file spends 1.2ms in Monaco model creation.
